<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via phoneNumber (symbol, a field of const object PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES), phoneNumber (literal, a string literal in actions))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx`  _(via phoneNumber (symbol, a field of const object PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES), phoneNumber (literal, a string literal in actions))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via phoneNumber (symbol, a field of const object PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES), phoneNumber (literal, a string literal in actions))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6cbdef1e4418d1ba62e3f93e9299fe8db953aaa8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0fb8c97c40e475b1024f94a88db414be819336ad` — the merge of head `9684fb3ba196ca4e8fd9a31ed3bffe40cac30ba8` into base `6cbdef1e4418d1ba62e3f93e9299fe8db953aaa8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0fb8c97c40e475b1024f94a88db414be819336ad && git checkout 0fb8c97c40e475b1024f94a88db414be819336ad
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6cbdef1e4418d1ba62e3f93e9299fe8db953aaa8 9684fb3ba196ca4e8fd9a31ed3bffe40cac30ba8 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6cbdef1e4418d1ba62e3f93e9299fe8db953aaa8 && git merge --no-ff 9684fb3ba196ca4e8fd9a31ed3bffe40cac30ba8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6cbdef1e4418d1ba62e3f93e9299fe8db953aaa8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6cbdef1e4418d1ba62e3f93e9299fe8db953aaa8` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2310b3028baa8116a7c14c01be43b2a10d8319ce`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts + packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/feature-gate-guard.test.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/action-params.zod.ts (`validateActionParams`), packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts (`resolveDeclaredActionParams`, `enforceActionParams`, the api forward), packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts (the REST `/actions` door), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts (`getPublicConfig`), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-user-endpoints.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/ActionParamDialog.tsx (`filterVisibleParams`, `refusalParamMarks`, `handleSubmit`), ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/AppContent.tsx (`features`), ui/packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx (the api door). The rest of the diff (the changeset, the two new test files) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Inputs: card #28280 (body, triage 6538087552, claim 6558617122, os-dev-report 6559354696), PR #28707 body, file list and net diff at the head above, the head's check-runs, and the live tree at `origin/main` `da6f0ce35da6` read with `git show`. Check-runs at read time: 24 completed (success or skipped, none failed; Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate, Auto Label, Check PR Size all success), 19 still `in_progress` (Build Core, Build UI Deps, Test Core 1-8, Live E2E UI, every Lint and Type Check lane). That is an honest reading, not a verdict on those lanes: no gate had answered red when this record was rendered.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set of the action door — NARROWED, and the PR does not say so. WRONG.** `sys_user.create_user` is a declared same-origin `type: 'api'` action, so a Console click goes through `POST /api/v1/actions/sys_user/create_user` (`useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx` 425-440, as #28649 measured), and both doors run the ADR-0104 D2 param contract BEFORE the in-process forward (`domains/actions.ts` 738; `action-execution.ts` 3753 then 3879). `resolveDeclaredActionParams` (`action-execution.ts` 2797-2815) emits one descriptor per declared param, in order, named `p.name ?? p.field`: with this diff that is `email` (required false) then `email` (required true). `validateActionParams` (`action-params.zod.ts` 185-193) folds them into `declared = new Map(); for (const p of resolved) declared.set(p.name, p)` — the LAST declaration wins, so the door's contract for `email` is `required: true`, unconditionally. `enforceActionParams` reads no `visible` and no `features`. Result on the tree: every bag without a present `email` is refused `400` with `Invalid action params: Action param "email" is required`, whatever phone sign-in says — including the phone-only create the endpoint accepts (`admin-user-endpoints.ts` 700-727) and the PR's own second scenario (phone sign-in on, Email optional, Phone Number filled). Before this diff the door passed that bag through. This is a server-side accept-set narrowing hidden behind a UI change; neither the PR body nor the changeset names it, and `Clause-②: no` is false for the tree as it stands (see ②). The PR's tests cannot see it: the app-shell test mocks the fetch at `authFetchSpy` (the door is never run), and the platform-objects pin evaluates gates only. Must-fix, in ④.
2. **Registry booking `sys_user.actions.create_user.params.email` under `phoneNumber.gatedInputs` — RIGHT as a booking.** `phoneNumber` is `opt-in`, so `featureGatePredicate('phoneNumber')` is `features.phoneNumber == true`. The forward guard resolves the path to the first param whose `name ?? field` equals the path's last segment (`resolveGatedInput`, `feature-gate-guard.test.ts` 122) — the FIRST `email` param, which carries exactly that gate through `requiresFeature` lowering (`lowerRequiresFeature`, no existing `visible`, so `source` is string-equal to the gate). The reverse guard's walker matches `features\.([A-Za-z0-9_]+)` over every param's `visible.source`, so it books three references (`features.phoneNumber == true`; `has(features.phoneNumber)`; `features.phoneNumber != true`) all under the one path, all found in the set. Neither guard's logic is edited; the diff to `feature-gate-guard.test.ts` is header prose only, so nothing is weakened. What the registry cannot say — and now silently does not — is that the SECOND param on the same path carries the negation; the row itself carries no note (should-fix, ④).
3. **Console rendering per `features` binding — RIGHT, with the default case marked.** `getPublicConfig()` always serves `phoneNumber: (pluginConfig as any).phoneNumber ?? false` (`auth-manager.ts` 4620), a boolean on every deployment. `AppContent.tsx` 298-311 holds `features` as `{}` until `getAuthConfig()` resolves, then `setFeatures(cfg.features ?? {})` whole; the Setup → Users page renders inside that provider (`AppContent.tsx` 1428; `HomeLayout`'s empty `features` is the Home surface only). `filterVisibleParams` (`ActionParamDialog.tsx` 244-280) shows a param whose gate answers `true` or faults. So: default deployment after the fetch → `{ phoneNumber: false }` → `has()` true, `!= true` true → the REQUIRED param alone is shown, marked, and a blank one is refused client-side (`handleSubmit` 596-600). Phone sign-in on → the optional param alone, beside Phone Number. Before the fetch answers, or when it fails → `{}` → the optional param alone, unmarked, as on `main` today. The card's bug (default case unmarked) is fixed at the dialog; the `has()` deviation from the order's bare spelling is the right call, since a bare `features.phoneNumber != true` on `{}` faults and the fail-open rule would draw BOTH Email inputs (A2/U2 in the report agree with the code read).
4. **Exactly one email submitted — RIGHT.** The dialog collects and serializes `visibleParams` only (`serializeParamValues(visibleParams, values)`, 610), and both params share the key `email`, so the bag carries one `email` whichever is shown.
5. **#28649's server-refusal marks — RIGHT, when the server is reached.** `refusalParamMarks` (158-172) marks a `required` entry whose `field` is in `collected`, built from `visibleParams` names; the shown param is named `email`, so the endpoint's `fields: [{ field: 'email', code: 'required' }]` still lands on the input. But under finding 1 the door's 400 arrives first, as a bare sentence with no `fields[]`, so with phone sign-in on the dialog shows the English `Invalid action params…` box instead of the #28649 mark — a regression of #28649's second case (phone on marks Email and Phone Number) on the live door.
6. **Endpoint refusal unchanged — RIGHT.** No server file is in the diff; `admin-user-endpoints.ts` 717-725 still answers `Email is required` / `Email or phone number is required` with per-field entries.
7. **Declared public surface of `@objectstack/spec` — one tuple literal widened.** `PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES.phoneNumber.gatedInputs` is `as const`, so the `.d.ts` literal type gains one member; no export added or removed (`check:api-surface` green locally, CI lane in progress). Precedent: fc4ac58 shipped the same kind of booking as `patch`, `Clause-②: no`.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/28280-create-user-email-required-mark.md`: `@objectstack/platform-objects` patch, `@objectstack/spec` patch. Both ship `dist`; the spec kernel chunk carries the new path. For the registry line alone, patch matches precedent (fc4ac58) and is right.
- `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none` on the PR body and the changeset: `Metadata-protocol: none` is right (no authorable key, value or meaning changes; `requiresFeature` and `visible` are existing keys). `Clause-②: no` is **wrong for the tree as it stands**: finding ① 1 narrows what `POST /api/v1/actions/sys_user/create_user` (and the MCP `run_action` door, same `enforceActionParams`) accepts — a phone-only bag that passed on `main` is refused at the door. A narrowing is `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and BREAKING, with an ADR-0087 disposition, which no one wants for a p3 mark; the right outcome is a tree that does not narrow (④ must-fix), after which `Clause-②: no` and patch stand as declared.
- `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` was NOT MEASURED locally (exit 3, needs every package `dist`). CI covers it: it is a step of ci.yml's `Build Core` job (line 3036), whose paths filter lists the script and every package source (line 408), and `Build Core` is `in_progress` on this head. The gate's verdict is CI's to give; the local non-measurement is honest and not a finding.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation 1 (`has(features.phoneNumber) &&` added to the order's bare `!= true`): **answered, accepted.** The code read in ① 3 agrees: on `{}` the bare gate faults, the dialog's fail-open rule shows the faulting param, and two Email inputs render. The `has()` term keeps the order's own hypothesis (one Email input) true in that state; the precedent spelling in `sys-user.page.ts` is the same shape. The first, optional param keeps the canonical gate the forward guard resolves, so option 1 is still option 1.
- Dev deviation 2 (reverse-guard red cited from the card, not re-run): **answered, accepted.** The reverse guard's walker and the booking are read above; the three rows are green on the head by the report, and the guard logic is untouched.
- Dev deviation 3 (model-free commit trailers): not a contract matter; noted only.
- `open_questions: []`, `out_of_scope_findings: []`: nothing to escalate from the report. One boundary the report did not flag and this record raises: the action door's param contract (① 1). It was not in the order's file surface and the order forbade a runtime change, so it is escalated to the seat as the must-fix below rather than judged as a dev omission.
- Triage's one-PR exception for `public-auth-features.ts` is honoured: the file changes by one value, no model change, and the guard header states the one-path, two-param booking as triage asked.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts`** — judged against the registry's own contract (its header: every `gatedInputs` path "must carry the matching predicate"; the forward and reverse guards in `feature-gate-guard.test.ts`) and its first consumers (`lowerRequiresFeature`, the guards, and the declaration in `sys-user.object.ts` the booking now stands for).

- **MUST-FIX — the two-param declaration the booking certifies narrows the action door's accept set** (① 1). The registry line is only true of the declaration in `sys-user.object.ts`, and that declaration, read by `resolveDeclaredActionParams` + `validateActionParams`, makes `email` unconditionally required at `POST /api/v1/actions/sys_user/create_user` and at MCP `run_action`: `validateActionParams` keys descriptors by name and keeps the last, which is the required param. Concretely on the head: phone sign-in on, an administrator fills Phone Number and leaves the optional Email blank → the door answers `400 Invalid action params: Action param "email" is required` before plugin-auth runs; the endpoint's own `Email or phone number is required` + `fields[]` never arrives, so #28649's mark is lost too; a REST or MCP caller creating a phone-only user is refused where `main` accepts. The order's hypothesis ("the server interface is unchanged", PR body 风险与回滚) does not hold. The fix is the seat's call, and every route is outside this PR's declared file surface: (a) make the dispatch contract read the two declarations as one param whose `required` is the AND of both (a `validateActionParams` / `resolveDeclaredActionParams` change, `packages/spec` ui surface, contract review again), (b) drop the server-visible second declaration and carry the required mark another way, or (c) the card's option 2 (a required-when predicate), which triage set aside at p3. Whichever is chosen, the PR must either keep the door's accept set identical to `main` and prove it with a door-level test (a `boot({ answer })` harness on `api-action-forward.test.ts` with the real `SysUser` declaration and a phone-only bag), or declare the narrowing honestly. As it stands: FAIL.
- **SHOULD-FIX — the booking row carries no note of what it stands for.** The registry header and the `gatedInputs` docblock still promise that each path's target "carries the matching predicate", and the forward guard enforces that on the first `email` param only; the second param's `features.phoneNumber != true` is exactly the predicate a `hide-when-on` flag lowers to, booked under an `opt-in` flag. The guard header and the pin explain it, but the registry is the file a reader opens first. One comment on the row (`// Two params on this path (#28280): the first carries this gate; the second is NEGATIVELY gated and pinned in platform-objects identity/sys-user-create-user-email-required.test.ts`) keeps the file self-describing, inside triage's one-PR exception.
- **SHOULD-FIX — the pre-fetch / failed-fetch state is unmarked, and nothing says so to the administrator.** With `features` `{}` the dialog draws the optional param and the endpoint still refuses a blank email. That is `main`'s behaviour, not a regression, and the window is short (the fetch starts at `AppContent` mount); but the PR body's 风险与回滚 says the dialog marks Email "未开启手机号登录（默认）时", which is true only after `/auth/config` has answered. State it in the changeset body (it already does, one line) and in the 维护者速读; no code change asked.
- The guard-test edit is prose only and weakens neither direction (① 2). The `has()` spelling is right (③). The client submits one `email` (① 4). The endpoint is untouched (① 6).

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-5fg7d3`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5kE5BrPUPNMMyv6oCH`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9684fb3ba196ca4e8fd9a31ed3bffe40cac30ba8`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/action-params.zod.ts + packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts (`resolveDeclaredActionParams`, `enforceActionParams`, the MCP `run_action` path), packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts (the REST `/actions` door), packages/runtime/src/domains/api-action-create-user-email-param.test.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/action-params.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/feature-gate-guard.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-user-endpoints.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-action-dispatch-contract.ts, docs/adr/0104-field-runtime-value-shape-contract.md. The rest of the diff (the changeset, the platform-objects pin, the app-shell test) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Delta record extending the base record on `2310b302` (PR comment 6559443163). Inputs: the base record; `git diff 2310b302 9684fb3b` (5 files, +206/-9: action-params.zod.ts, action-params.test.ts, public-auth-features.ts, the new runtime door test, the changeset); the live PR body at this head (both declaration lines rewritten); the dev's round-2 os-dev-report 6560214983 and the claim amendment 6560238686 on #28280; the head's check-runs at read time. Everything in the base record not restated here stands as judged there.

Check-runs on `9684fb3b` at read time: every lane completed; `Check Changeset` ran twice — the 14:59Z run failed against the old PR body (`Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none` against a changeset that now says `yes (widening)` / `semantic`), the 15:50Z run on the patched body is `success`. Every other completed run is `success` or `skipped` (Build Core, Test Core 1-8, Test UI 1-16, Live E2E UI, every Lint and Type Check lane, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards, Dogfood Regression Gate). The stale failure row is the only non-green conclusion on the head, and the newer run of the same gate supersedes it. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, NOT MEASURED locally (exit 3 again), is a step of `Build Core`, which is `success` on this head: the gate is measured by CI.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The must-fix of the base record — CLOSED, in the tree.** `validateActionParams` (`action-params.zod.ts` 201-208) now folds same-name descriptors as `declared.set(name, first ? { ...first, required: Boolean(first.required && p.required) } : p)`: a name is required only when EVERY declaration of it is required, and the value shape (type, multiple, options) is the FIRST declaration's. `resolveDeclaredActionParams` (unchanged, `action-execution.ts` 2788-2810) still emits both `email` descriptors in order (`required` false, then true), so the folded `email` is `required: false`, type `email`. `enforceActionParams` is the only caller (`action-execution.ts` 2877), reached from the REST door (`domains/actions.ts` 738) and the in-process/MCP path (`action-execution.ts` 3753); no other code on the head calls `validateActionParams` or `resolveDeclaredActionParams` (grep over packages/ and ui/: the remaining hits are prose in `packages/lint/src/validate-action-dispatch-contract.ts`, `screen-input-contract.ts`, `action.zod.ts`, an ADR and two READMEs, none of which states a last-wins or unique-name rule). So on the head: phone sign-in on, phone-only bag → the door passes it and forwards it to plugin-auth; phone sign-in off, blank email → the door passes it and the ENDPOINT's `400 VALIDATION_FAILED "Email is required"` with `fields[]` is relayed whole (`admin-user-endpoints.ts` 717-725, untouched), so #28649's per-field mark is restored on the live door; a non-string `email` is still refused at the door by the first declaration's `email` value shape. The accept set of the door for `sys_user.create_user` is `main`'s again, and the endpoint stays the judge, which is the right split: the door reads neither `visible` nor `features` and cannot know which declaration the caller saw.
2. **Nothing else relied on last-wins — VERIFIED, as far as a text census goes.** The dev reports an AST census (objectstack 430 arrays incl. ui/ and examples/, hotcrm 7, JSON 2) finding only `create_user`'s `email`. This record re-ran an independent text-level census (every `params: [` / `actionParams: [` array literal in .ts/.tsx/.js/.mjs/.json/.yaml under the tree, top-level entries keyed by `name` or `field`) over the whole objectstack tree at `9684fb3b` and hotcrm `origin/main`: 296 keyed arrays in objectstack, 7 in hotcrm, exactly one repeat — `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts:315 email x2`. The two censuses count arrays differently (the AST pass counts arrays with no keyed entries too) and agree on the one finding. Not covered by either: params arrays assembled at runtime or stored in `sys_metadata` rows by a deployment; for those the change is a widening (a bag refused before is accepted now; nothing accepted before is refused), which is the direction the declaration names.
3. **The new door test (`packages/runtime/src/domains/api-action-create-user-email-param.test.ts`) — adequate for the must-fix.** It drives `HttpDispatcher.handleActions('/sys_user/create_user', 'POST', …)` with the REAL `SysUser` declaration over a recording in-process target (the `api-action-forward.test.ts` harness shape), so `enforceActionParams` → `resolveDeclaredActionParams` → `validateActionParams` run on the real two-param declaration, and the forward to `/api/v1/auth/admin/create-user` is observed. Cases: the declaration carries [false, true]; phone-only passes and is forwarded with `generatePassword: true`; blank email passes the door and the endpoint's 400 (`fields[]` included) is relayed; an email is forwarded; a non-string email is refused at the door with nothing forwarded. Red-first on the base head is reported (2 of 5 red with the exact `Action param "email" is required` sentence this record predicted) and the merge was ablated back to red. The MCP `run_action` path is not driven, and that is right: `create_user` declares no `ai.exposed`, so `systemObjectActionExposureError` refuses it before `enforceActionParams` (`action-execution.ts` 3634ff, measured by the dev), and both doors share the one `enforceActionParams`. The spec-level pins in `action-params.test.ts` (optional-then-required and reversed → no issue; both required → `required`; first declaration's option set judges the value) cover the fold's three branches.
4. **Public surface of `@objectstack/spec` — one exported function's semantics change, no signature change.** `validateActionParams` keeps its signature and export; `check:api-surface` has nothing to record; the Type Check lanes are green. The registry row change is as in the base record (literal tuple widened; patch precedent fc4ac58).
5. **ADR-0104 D2 — not reversed.** D2 declares `params[]` a complete value contract enforced before the handler; it says nothing about a name declared twice (no "unique", "duplicate" or last-wins sentence in `docs/adr/0104-…`), so the fold is a definition where there was none, not a reversal needing an ADR (Prime Directive #13). The docblock in `action-params.zod.ts` records the rule and its reason beside the code.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset at head: `@objectstack/spec` **minor**, `@objectstack/platform-objects` patch; `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: semantic`; PR body carries the same two lines and `Check Changeset` on the patched body is green.
- **Right level.** `Metadata-protocol: semantic` is the honest kind: the meaning of `params[].required` on a twice-declared name changes at the doors (what an author wrote is read differently), and a kind takes at least `minor` on the package the diff moves — the fold lives in `packages/spec/src/ui`, so spec `minor`; platform-objects publishes no protocol change of its own (two declarations under existing keys) and keeps `patch`. `Clause-②: yes (widening)`: the doors' accept set grows (a twice-declared name with one optional declaration no longer requires the key) and nothing previously accepted is refused — no narrowing arm, no BREAKING banner, no ADR-0087 disposition owed. Round 1's `no` / `none` / patch was wrong for round 1's tree (the base record's ② finding) and is withdrawn by this re-declaration.
